corrected_fields.summary: The Federal Reserve submitted its July 2018 Monetary Policy Report to Congress, reaffirming its dual mandate of maximum employment and stable prices (2% PCE inflation target). The document states the median FOMC participant estimate for longer-run normal unemployment is 4.6 percent. The Committee commits to a balanced approach when employment and inflation objectives are not complementary. Source data extends through Q1 2018 and was publicly available as of July 12, 2018. Note: This record covers the introductory sections only (transmittal letter, statement on longer-run goals and monetary policy strategy).
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This quarterly report establishes the Federal Reserve's official policy framework and strategic principles as of mid-2018. It documents the Fed's commitment to a 2% symmetric inflation target, which anchors long-term inflation expectations. The stated longer-run unemployment estimate of 4.6% provides a benchmark for assessing labor market slack. This document serves as a foundational reference for understanding Fed policy intentions and communication strategy. Historical record from July 2018.
corrected_fields.macro_context: As a quarterly Monetary Policy Report submitted to Congress pursuant to section 2B of the Federal Reserve Act, this document provides the official framework for monetary policy. It describes the Fed's commitment to price stability (2% PCE inflation symmetric target) and its flexible approach to maximum employment. The balance of risks assessment and the dual mandate framework described here inform the trajectory of monetary policy decisions during the reported period. Historical document from mid-2018.
